title: 07. Google ADK: Day 15 — Deployment & Capstone: Cloud Run, Agent Engine & Production
summary: An agent that runs in your notebook is a demo. An agent that runs in production is a product — and the gap between the two is everything that happens between adk run and a public URL.

sections.title: 1. Why Deployment Matters
sections.body:
An agent that runs in your notebook is a demo. An agent that runs in production is a *product* — and the gap between the two is everything that happens between `adk run` and a public URL. Production agents need persistent session storage (so a refresh doesn't wipe the conversation), artifact storage (so generated PDFs survive container restarts), observability (so you can debug why the agent gave a wrong answer three hours ago), error recovery (so a rate-limit doesn't surface as a 500), guardrails (so a malicious user can't `delete_user` themselves out of your database), and an evaluation gate (so a prompt change doesn't silently degrade quality).

ADK v2.7.0 ships four first-class deployment paths. **Cloud Run** is the recommended default for Python — `adk deploy cloud_run` containerizes your `agents/` folder, wires persistent storage, and gives you a public HTTPS URL in under five minutes. **Agent Runtime** (formerly "Vertex AI Agent Engine") is the fully-managed option for event-driven agents triggered by Pub/Sub or Eventarc. **GKE** is for teams already running Kubernetes who want ADK to fit their existing infrastructure. **Custom FastAPI** via `get_fast_api_app()` is the escape hatch when you need full control — auth middleware, custom routes, or non-Google-Cloud deployment.

The capstone at the end of today combines *everything* from Days 01–14: multi-agent coordination with sub-agents, async tools, Pydantic output schemas, session state with `output_key`, SQLite persistent sessions, GCS artifact storage, `before_model_callback` guardrails, `after_tool_callback` audit logging, `on_model_error_callback` recovery, and a deploy-ready FastAPI server. By the end of this notebook, you'll have a complete, production-shaped agent system you can drop into a real product. This is the final day of the 15-day course — and the first day of your ADK building journey.

💡 Key Concept

**Deployment is not the last step — it's the step that exposes every shortcut you took.** An agent that worked in dev but loses state on restart tells you instantly that you used `InMemorySessionService`. An agent that 500s under load tells you you forgot rate limiting. An agent that gives flaky answers tells you your eval gate was weak. Production is the truth serum for everything you've built.

sections.title: 2. Core Concepts
sections.body:
### 2.1 The Four Deployment Options

ADK v2.7.0 supports four first-class deployment targets. Each has a clear sweet spot — pick based on your hosting constraint, not on fashion.

| Target | Best for | CLI command | SLA | Infra burden |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Cloud Run** | Python HTTP agents (recommended default) | `adk deploy cloud_run` | Google Cloud SLA | Zero (serverless) |
| **Agent Runtime (Agent Engine)** | Event-driven, fully managed | `adk deploy agent_engine` | Google Cloud SLA | Zero (fully managed) |
| **GKE** | Enterprises on Kubernetes | `adk deploy gke` | Your cluster's SLA | High (you manage K8s) |
| **Custom FastAPI** | Any cloud, full control | `uvicorn main:app` | Yours | Medium (you manage hosting) |

```
              DEPLOYMENT DECISION TREE — pick the right runtime
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                          │
│   Do you need Google Cloud SLA + fully managed infra?                    │
│       │                                                                  │
│       ├─ YES ─► Do you want event-driven (Pub/Sub, Eventarc) triggers?   │
│       │            │                                                     │
│       │            ├─ YES ─► ① Agent Runtime (Agent Engine)              │
│       │            │           adk deploy agent_engine                   │
│       │            │           --trigger_sources=pubsub,eventarc         │
│       │            │                                                     │
│       │            └─ NO  ─► ② Cloud Run  (recommended for Python)       │
│       │                        adk deploy cloud_run                      │
│       │                        --with_ui                                  │
│       │                                                                  │
│       └─ NO  ─► Do you run Kubernetes already?                          │
│                    │                                                     │
│                    ├─ YES ─► ③ GKE  (adk deploy gke)                    │
│                    │                                                     │
│                    └─ NO  ─► ④ Custom FastAPI                           │
│                                from google.adk.cli.fast_api import       │
│                                    get_fast_api_app                      │
│                                # + uvicorn / Docker / any cloud          │
│                                                                          │
│   Service URI schemes (used by every deploy command):                   │
│     Sessions:   agentengine://<id>    sqlite+aiosqlite:///path.db       │
│                 memory://              <any SQLAlchemy URL>              │
│     Artifacts:  gs://<bucket>          file://<path>    memory://        │
│     Memory:     rag://<corpus_id>      agentengine://<id>  memory://     │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 2.2 Cloud Run — the Recommended Default

Cloud Run is Google's serverless container platform. `adk deploy cloud_run` packages your agent into a container, uploads it to Artifact Registry, and creates a Cloud Run service with sensible defaults (HTTPS URL, autoscaling, configurable concurrency). It's the fastest path from `agents/` folder to public URL.

```bash
adk deploy cloud_run \
  --project=$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT \
  --region=$GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION \
  --service_name=$SERVICE_NAME \
  --app_name=$APP_NAME \
  --with_ui \
  --session_service_uri="agentengine://<agent_engine_id>" \
  --artifact_service_uri="gs://<bucket_name>" \
  --memory_service_uri="rag://<rag_corpus_id>" \
  $AGENT_PATH
```

Pass gcloud flags after `--`:

```bash
adk deploy cloud_run --project=... --region=... path/to/my_agent \
  -- --no-allow-unauthenticated --min-instances=2 --max-instances=100
```

Full options: `--project`, `--region`, `--service_name` (default `adk-default-service-name`), `--app_name`, `--port` (default 8000), `--with_ui`, `--allow_origins`, `--session_service_uri`, `--artifact_service_uri`, `--memory_service_uri`, `--otel_to_cloud`, `--trace_to_cloud`, `--temp_folder`.

💡 Key Concept

**Service URI schemes are the lingua franca of ADK deployment.** Every command that touches storage (`adk run`, `adk web`, `adk api_server`, `adk deploy cloud_run`, `adk deploy agent_engine`) accepts the same URI format. Sessions use `agentengine://`, `memory://`, `sqlite+aiosqlite://`, or any SQLAlchemy URL. Artifacts use `gs://`, `file://`, `memory://`. Memory uses `rag://`, `agentengine://`, `memory://`. Pick once per environment (dev/staging/prod), reuse across commands.

### 2.3 Agent Runtime (Agent Engine) — Fully Managed

ADK 2.x renamed "Vertex AI Agent Engine" to **Agent Runtime** (part of Google Cloud Agent Platform). The CLI command is still `adk deploy agent_engine` for backward compatibility. Agent Runtime is for event-driven agents — it exposes `/trigger/*` endpoints that Pub/Sub or Eventarc can hit directly, without you managing a server.

```bash
# Express Mode (API key — no Google Cloud project required)
adk deploy agent_engine --api_key=[api_key] my_agent

# Google Cloud Project (full feature set)
adk deploy agent_engine \
  --project=[project] \
  --region=[region] \
  --display_name=[app_name] \
  --agent_engine_id=[optional_existing_id] \
  --otel_to_cloud \
  --trigger_sources=pubsub,eventarc \
  my_agent
```

Full options: `--api_key`, `--project`, `--region`, `--agent_engine_id`, `--display_name`, `--description`, `--otel_to_cloud`, `--trigger_sources` (registers `/trigger/*` endpoints), `--adk_version` (default `'2.6.0'`), `--extra_packages`, `--session_service_uri`, `--artifact_service_uri`, `--memory_service_uri`, `--agent_engine_config_file`.

**Important**: Python Agent Runtime deployment does *not* include the ADK API server / Web UI libraries — Agent Runtime provides them. Don't try to bundle `fastapi` or the web UI into your agent package; it'll bloat the deployable and the runtime provides equivalent surfaces.

🚀 Pro Tip

**Express Mode is the fastest way to test Agent Runtime.** `adk deploy agent_engine --api_key=$GOOGLE_API_KEY my_agent` skips project setup, IAM, and service account creation. Use it for prototyping; switch to project-mode (`--project`, `--region`) when you need Cloud Trace, Eventarc triggers, or persistent Agent Engine IDs across deploys.

### 2.4 GKE — for Kubernetes-Native Teams

`adk deploy gke` deploys your agent to a Google Kubernetes Engine cluster. It generates the Deployment, Service, and HorizontalPodAutoscaler manifests, applies them via `kubectl`, and returns the LoadBalancer URL. Use this when your team already operates GKE and wants ADK to fit existing observability, networking, and security infrastructure.

```bash
adk deploy gke \
  --project=$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT \
  --region=$GOOGLE_CLOUD_LOCATION \
  --cluster_name=$CLUSTER_NAME \
  --service_name=$SERVICE_NAME \
  $AGENT_PATH
```

GKE deployment is the highest-effort option — you're responsible for cluster autoscaling, node pool management, ingress configuration, and certificate renewal. Only choose it if your org already has GKE investment; otherwise Cloud Run gives you 90% of the benefit at 10% of the operational cost.

### 2.5 Custom FastAPI — `get_fast_api_app()`

When you need full control — custom auth middleware, non-Google-Cloud deployment (AWS, Azure, on-prem), or integration with an existing FastAPI app — use `get_fast_api_app()` to embed ADK's full REST surface in your own ASGI app.

```python
# main.py
import os
import uvicorn
from google.adk.cli.fast_api import get_fast_api_app

AGENT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SESSION_SERVICE_URI = "sqlite+aiosqlite:///./sessions.db"
ALLOWED_ORIGINS = ["http://localhost", "http://localhost:8080", "*"]
SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE = True

app = get_fast_api_app(
    agents_dir=AGENT_DIR,
    session_service_uri=SESSION_SERVICE_URI,
    allow_origins=ALLOWED_ORIGINS,
    web=SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE,
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0", port=int(os.environ.get("PORT", 8080)))
```

This gives you the same `/run`, `/run_sse`, `/list-apps`, sessions, and (optionally) Web UI endpoints as `adk web` — but as an importable `app` object you can compose with your own middleware, routes, and dependencies. Run with `uvicorn main:app` or wrap in a Docker container.

⚠️ Important

**v2.7.0 breaking change for BigQuery analytics.** `pyarrow` (~50 MB) moved out of the `[gcp]` extra into the new `[bigquery-analytics]` extra. If you previously relied on `BigQueryAgentAnalyticsPlugin` via `google-adk[gcp]`, you must now install `google-adk[bigquery-analytics]` explicitly. Otherwise you'll get `ImportError: pyarrow` when the plugin tries to write to BigQuery.

### 2.6 Observability — Five Layers

Production agents fail in subtle ways: wrong answers, slow turns, tool timeouts, malformed LLM outputs, silent state corruption. ADK provides five observability layers, each catching a different class of problem:

1. **`--trace_to_cloud`** — exports OpenTelemetry spans to Cloud Trace. Every LLM call, tool call, and event yield becomes a span. Searchable by trace ID, correlatable across services.
2. **`--otel_to_cloud`** — exports OpenTelemetry metrics to Cloud Monitoring. Counter for invocations, histogram for token counts, gauge for active sessions.
3. **`BigQueryAgentAnalyticsPlugin`** (v2.7.0) — ships every event to BigQuery for SQL analytics. Install with `pip install google-adk[bigquery-analytics]`. Query: "show me all sessions where the agent called `delete_user` in the last 7 days".
4. **`ReflectAndRetryModelPlugin`** (v2.6.0+) — self-heals malformed LLM responses. When the model returns broken JSON or invalid tool args, the plugin asks the model to *reflect on its error* and retry — often succeeds on attempt 2 with no user-visible failure.
5. **`LoggingPlugin`** — pretty-prints every event to stdout. The cheapest observability; essential for dev even if you have the others.

For non-Google-Cloud deployments, use OpenTelemetry's `OtlpGrpcSpanExporter` to ship traces to any OTLP-compatible backend (Jaeger, Tempo, Honeycomb, Datadog).

🚀 Pro Tip

**Stack the observability layers.** `--trace_to_cloud` for request debugging, `--otel_to_cloud` for SLO dashboards, `BigQueryAgentAnalyticsPlugin` for product analytics ("what % of sessions end with a successful booking?"), `ReflectAndRetryModelPlugin` for resilience, `LoggingPlugin` for dev. Cost is roughly proportional to value — LoggingPlugin is free, BigQuery analytics costs BigQuery storage (cheap), Cloud Trace/Monitoring have generous free tiers.

```
                PRODUCTION READINESS CHECKLIST
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                                                          │
│  □ PERSISTENT SESSIONS                                                   │
│    --session_service_uri="agentengine://<id>"                            │
│    OR  "sqlite+aiosqlite:///path.db"                                     │
│    OR  "postgresql+asyncpg://user:pass@host/db"                          │
│    NEVER ship with InMemorySessionService to production.                 │
│                                                                          │
│  □ ARTIFACT STORAGE                                                      │
│    --artifact_service_uri="gs://<bucket>"                                │
│    For PDFs, images, generated files — survives container restarts.      │
│                                                                          │
│  □ MEMORY SERVICE (cross-session recall)                                 │
│    --memory_service_uri="rag://<corpus_id>"                              │
│    Optional but transformative for support/sales agents.                 │
│                                                                          │
│  □ OBSERVABILITY                                                         │
│    --trace_to_cloud        (Cloud Trace — request spans)                 │
│    --otel_to_cloud         (Cloud Monitoring — metrics)                  │
│    plugins=[BigQueryAgentAnalyticsPlugin(...)]  (analytics warehouse)    │
│    plugins=[LoggingPlugin()]                     (console pretty-print)  │
│    plugins=[ReflectAndRetryModelPlugin()]        (self-heal bad outputs) │
│                                                                          │
│  □ ERROR HANDLING                                                        │
│    on_model_error_callback  (graceful LLM failures)                      │
│    on_tool_error_callback   (graceful tool failures)                     │
│    RetryConfig(max_attempts=3)  (framework-level retries)                │
│                                                                          │
│  □ GUARDRAILS                                                            │
│    before_model_callback   (profanity, PII, topic restriction)           │
│    before_tool_callback    (rate limit, auth check, audit log)           │
│                                                                          │
│  □ SCALING & AUTH                                                       │
│    Cloud Run: --min-instances=2 --max-instances=100                      │
│    Add --no-allow-unauthenticated (after testing)                        │
│    Front with Cloud Armor / API Gateway for WAF + API keys               │
│                                                                          │
│  □ EVALUATION GATE                                                       │
│    adk eval my_agent eval_sets/ --eval_storage_uri="gs://..."            │
│    Block deploys on regressions in CI/CD.                                │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: 4. Visual Diagram — Deployment Options Matrix
sections.body:
```python
from IPython.display import Image, display
display(Image(filename="images/day15_deployment_options.png"))
```

The four boxes across the top are the four deployment targets; each one has a "what it is" description (middle row) and "when to use it" guidance (bottom row). The service URI schemes at the top are universally accepted by every deploy command — pick once per environment, reuse everywhere.

Example 1: Deploy to Cloud Run

Full CLI command with persistent sessions, GCS artifacts, and observability

This is the recommended production path for Python ADK agents. The command below deploys the `my_agent` package to Cloud Run with three persistent storage layers and full observability — sessions survive container restarts (Agent Engine), generated artifacts go to GCS, cross-session memory uses Vertex AI RAG, and every request is traced.

Before running, ensure you've run `gcloud auth login` and `gcloud config set project $YOUR_PROJECT`, and that the required APIs are enabled (`run.googleapis.com`, `aiplatform.googleapis.com`, `storage.googleapis.com`). The first deploy takes ~3-5 minutes (container build + push); subsequent deploys are faster (cached layers).

```python
# Deploy to Cloud Run with full production config
adk deploy cloud_run \
    --project=$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT \
    --region=us-central1 \
    --service_name=travel-planner-svc \
    --app_name=travel_planner \
    --with_ui \
    --session_service_uri="agentengine://1234567890123456789" \
    --artifact_service_uri="gs://my-adk-artifacts/travel_planner/" \
    --memory_service_uri="rag://my-rag-corpus-12345" \
    --trace_to_cloud \
    --otel_to_cloud \
    ./travel_planner
```

**Output**

```text
\nBuilding container image...\n  Step 1/12 : FROM python:3.11-slim\n  Step 2/12 : WORKDIR /app\n  Step 3/12 : COPY requirements.txt .\n  Step 4/12 : RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt\n  Step 5/12 : COPY . .\n  ...\n  Step 12/12 : CMD exec uvicorn main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT\nPushing to Artifact Registry...\n  us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT/adk-images/travel_planner:latest\nDeploying to Cloud Run service 'travel-planner-svc'...\n  ✓ Service created (region: us-central1)\n  ✓ IAM policy set (allow unauthenticated for testing)\n  ✓ URL: https://travel-planner-svc-abc123.uc.a.run.app\n\nDeployment complete.\n  Web UI:        https://travel-planner-svc-abc123.uc.a.run.app\n  REST API:      https://travel-planner-svc-abc123.uc.a.run.app/run\n  SSE endpoint:  https://travel-planner-svc-abc123.uc.a.run.app/run_sse\n  Docs:          https://travel-planner-svc-abc123.uc.a.run.app/docs\n
```

### Hardening for production

The first deploy uses `--allow-unauthenticated` (the default) for easy testing. For production, flip to authenticated:

```bash
# Revoke public access
gcloud run services remove-iam-policy-binding travel-planner-svc \
  --member="allUsers" --role="roles/run.invoker"

# Set up min instances (avoid cold starts) and configure concurrency
gcloud run services update travel-planner-svc \
  --min-instances=2 --max-instances=100 --concurrency=80

# Front with API Gateway or Cloud Armor for API-key auth + WAF
gcloud api-gateway apis create travel-planner-api \
  --grpc-service-config=... 
```

Add the eval gate in your CI/CD pipeline before any deploy — block the deploy if `adk eval travel_planner eval_sets/` reports regressions vs. the last green build.

🚀 Pro Tip

**Pin your ADK version in production.** Add `google-adk==2.7.0` to your `requirements.txt` so deploys are reproducible. The `--adk_version` flag on `adk deploy agent_engine` defaults to `'2.6.0'` — explicitly set it to `2.7.0` to use the latest runtime.

Example 2: Deploy to Agent Engine (Express Mode)

Use API key auth — no Google Cloud project setup required

Express Mode is the fastest way to get an agent onto Google's managed runtime. Pass a Gemini API key, point at your agent folder, and Agent Engine handles containerization, scaling, and HTTPS URL generation. No project config, no IAM, no service account — just an API key (get one free at `aistudio.google.com/apikey`).

Express Mode is great for prototyping, demos, and internal tools. When you need production features — Cloud Trace, Eventarc triggers, persistent Agent Engine IDs across redeploys, VPC-SC controls — switch to project mode (`--project`, `--region`).

```python
# Deploy to Agent Engine in Express Mode
adk deploy agent_engine \
    --api_key=$GOOGLE_API_KEY \
    --display_name="Customer Support Agent v1" \
    --description="Handles tier-1 customer support queries" \
    --otel_to_cloud \
    ./customer_support_agent
```

**Output**

```text
\nValidating agent package...\n  ✓ Found root_agent in customer_support_agent/agent.py\n  ✓ 4 tools detected: lookup_order, refund_order, escalate_to_human, faq_search\n\nPackaging agent for Agent Runtime...\n  ✓ Requirements: google-adk==2.7.0, litellm>=1.84, httpx\n  ✓ Extra packages: [none]\n\nUploading to Agent Engine (Express Mode)...\n  ✓ Agent Engine ID: 9876543210987654321\n  ✓ Display name: Customer Support Agent v1\n  ✓ Status: READY\n\nTrigger endpoints:\n  POST https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com/v1/projects/...\n       /agents/9876543210987654321:run\n  POST .../agents/9876543210987654321:runSse\n\nExpress Mode ready. To upgrade to project mode with Cloud Trace\nand Eventarc triggers, redeploy with --project and --region.\n
```

### Project mode for production

```bash
adk deploy agent_engine \
  --project=$GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT \
  --region=us-central1 \
  --display_name="Customer Support Agent v1" \
  --agent_engine_id=9876543210987654321 \
  --otel_to_cloud \
  --trigger_sources=pubsub,eventarc \
  --adk_version=2.7.0 \
  ./customer_support_agent
```

`--agent_engine_id` reuses an existing Agent Engine instance (instead of creating a new one) — important for stable trigger URLs across redeploys. `--trigger_sources=pubsub,eventarc` registers `/trigger/pubsub` and `/trigger/eventarc` endpoints; wire a Pub/Sub topic or Eventarc trigger to those URLs to invoke the agent on schedule or external event.

💡 Key Concept

**Event-driven agents are Agent Runtime's superpower.** Wire a Pub/Sub topic to `https://.../trigger/pubsub` and every message published invokes the agent. Use cases: a support agent that fires when a Zendesk ticket is created; a fraud-detection agent that fires on every transaction above $10k; an inventory agent that fires when stock drops below threshold. No server, no queue consumer, no boilerplate — just an Agent Engine ID and a trigger URL.

Example 3: Custom FastAPI Server

Full main.py with get_fast_api_app, persistent SQLite, and CORS

When Cloud Run / Agent Runtime don't fit — non-Google-Cloud deployment, custom auth middleware, integration with an existing FastAPI app — `get_fast_api_app()` gives you the same REST surface as `adk web` as an importable ASGI app. Below is a complete `main.py` ready to run with `uvicorn` or wrap in Docker.

The pattern is: import `get_fast_api_app`, pass it your `agents_dir` (folder containing agent packages), `session_service_uri` (SQLite for simplicity — swap for Postgres in prod), `allow_origins` (CORS), and `web=True` to also serve the Web UI. Add your own routes/middleware before or after — `app` is a standard FastAPI instance.

```python
# main.py — Custom FastAPI server with ADK
import os
import logging
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.middleware import Middleware
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from google.adk.cli.fast_api import get_fast_api_app

# ── Configuration ───────────────────────────────────────────────
AGENT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
SESSION_SERVICE_URI = os.getenv(
    "SESSION_SERVICE_URI",
    "sqlite+aiosqlite:///./sessions.db",  # swap for postgres in prod
)
ARTIFACT_SERVICE_URI = os.getenv(
    "ARTIFACT_SERVICE_URI",
    "file://./artifacts/",  # swap for gs://bucket in prod
)
ALLOWED_ORIGINS = os.getenv(
    "ALLOWED_ORIGINS",
    "http://localhost,http://localhost:3000,http://localhost:8080",
).split(",")
SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE = os.getenv("SERVE_WEB_UI", "true").lower() == "true"

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger("adk.server")

# ── Build the ADK FastAPI app ──────────────────────────────────
app: FastAPI = get_fast_api_app(
    agents_dir=AGENT_DIR,
    session_service_uri=SESSION_SERVICE_URI,
    artifact_service_uri=ARTIFACT_SERVICE_URI,
    allow_origins=ALLOWED_ORIGINS,
    web=SERVE_WEB_INTERFACE,
)

# ── Custom middleware (runs BEFORE ADK routes) ─────────────────
@app.middleware("http")
async def add_request_id_and_log(request: Request, call_next):
    """Tag every request with an ID for log correlation."""
    import uuid
    request_id = request.headers.get("X-Request-ID", str(uuid.uuid4()))
    logger.info(f"[{request_id}] {request.method} {request.url.path}")
    response = await call_next(request)
    response.headers["X-Request-ID"] = request_id
    return response

# ── Custom routes (compose with ADK's /run, /run_sse, etc.) ────
@app.get("/health")
async def health_check():
    """Liveness probe for container orchestration."""
    return {
        "status": "ok",
        "agent_dir": AGENT_DIR,
        "session_backend": SESSION_SERVICE_URI.split("://")[0],
    }

@app.get("/version")
async def version():
    """Version endpoint for deploy tracking."""
    import google.adk
    return {
        "adk_version": google.adk.__version__,
        "app_name": os.path.basename(AGENT_DIR),
    }

# ── Run with uvicorn (or wrap in Docker + gunicorn) ────────────
if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(
        app,
        host="0.0.0.0",
        port=int(os.environ.get("PORT", 8080)),
        log_level="info",
    )
```


### Dockerfile

Wrap the FastAPI app in a container for any-cloud deployment:

```dockerfile
FROM python:3.11-slim

WORKDIR /app

# Install ADK + extras
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

# Copy agent code
COPY . .

# Expose port (Cloud Run sets $PORT)
ENV PORT=8080
EXPOSE 8080

# Run with gunicorn + uvicorn workers (production-grade)
CMD exec gunicorn --bind :$PORT --workers 2 --worker-class uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker main:app
```

Build and run locally: `docker build -t my-adk-agent . && docker run -p 8080:8080 my-adk-agent`. Deploy to any container platform (Cloud Run, AWS ECS, Azure Container Apps, Fly.io, Railway).

🚀 Pro Tip

**Use gunicorn with uvicorn workers in production**, not bare `uvicorn`. Uvicorn alone runs a single event loop — if one request blocks (sync I/O in a tool), the whole server stalls. Gunicorn spawns N worker processes (set `--workers` to `2 * CPU + 1`), so a slow request in worker A doesn't block worker B. Add `--worker-class uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker` to use uvicorn's ASGI transport inside gunicorn's process model.

Example 4: 🏆 CAPSTONE — Multi-Agent Travel Planner

4-agent system combining everything from Days 01–14: sub-agents, async tools, state, memory, artifacts, callbacks, FastAPI deploy

This is the capstone — a complete, deploy-ready travel planner that combines every concept from the course. It has a **coordinator agent** that delegates to three **single-turn sub-agents** (weather, flights, hotels), uses **async tools** for I/O-bound API calls, persists sessions to **SQLite**, stores generated itineraries as **GCS artifacts**, uses **InMemory memory** for cross-session recall (swap for `rag://` in prod), enforces **guardrails** via `before_model_callback`, **audits** tool calls via `after_tool_callback`, and **recovers gracefully** from LLM errors via `on_model_error_callback`. The whole thing is wrapped in a FastAPI server ready for Cloud Run.

Read the code top-to-bottom — every block is annotated with which day's concept it implements. By the time you finish, you'll have a template you can fork for any production multi-agent system.

💡 Key Concept

**Architecture: 1 coordinator + 3 sub-agents + 7 tools + 3 callbacks + persistent state.** The coordinator (`travel_planner`) routes user intent to sub-agents via `transfer_to_agent`. Each sub-agent (`weather_agent`, `flight_agent`, `hotel_agent`) is `mode="single_turn"` — runs once, returns a result, control flows back to the coordinator. Sub-agents share state via `output_key` (each saves its result to `session.state`), and the coordinator's final response aggregates them via Jinja2-style templating.

```python
# travel_planner/agent.py — CAPSTONE multi-agent travel planner
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Combines concepts from Days 01-14:
#   Day 02 — LlmAgent parameters & config
#   Day 04 — Function tools (sync + async)
#   Day 07 — Session state with output_key + prefix scopes
#   Day 08 — DatabaseSessionService (SQLite persistent)
#   Day 09 — GcsArtifactService (itinerary PDF), InMemoryMemoryService
#   Day 10 — Sub-agents (coordinator + 3 single_turn workers)
#   Day 13 — before_model_callback (guardrail),
#            after_tool_callback (audit log),
#            on_model_error_callback (recovery)
#   Day 15 — Deploy via get_fast_api_app() (see main.py below)

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import json
import time
import uuid
from copy import deepcopy
from typing import Any, Optional

from google.adk.agents.llm_agent import LlmAgent
from google.adk.agents.callback_context import CallbackContext
from google.adk.models import LlmRequest, LlmResponse
from google.adk.tools.tool_context import ToolContext
from google.adk.tools.base_tool import BaseTool
from google.genai import types

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# TOOLS (Day 04) — async for I/O-bound calls
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

async def get_weather(city: str, date: str) -> dict:
    """Fetch the weather forecast for a city on a specific date.

    Args:
        city: City name, e.g. "Tokyo".
        date: ISO date string YYYY-MM-DD.
    """
    await asyncio.sleep(0.2)  # simulate API latency
    mock = {
        "Tokyo": {"temp_c": 22, "condition": "Partly Cloudy", "humidity": 65},
        "London": {"temp_c": 14, "condition": "Rainy", "humidity": 80},
        "Paris": {"temp_c": 18, "condition": "Sunny", "humidity": 55},
    }
    w = mock.get(city, {"temp_c": 20, "condition": "Clear", "humidity": 60})
    return {"city": city, "date": date, **w, "source": "mock_weather_api"}

async def search_flights(origin: str, destination: str, date: str) -> dict:
    """Search for flights between two cities on a given date.

    Args:
        origin: Origin IATA code (e.g. "JFK").
        destination: Destination IATA code (e.g. "HND").
        date: Departure date YYYY-MM-DD.
    """
    await asyncio.sleep(0.3)
    return {
        "origin": origin,
        "destination": destination,
        "date": date,
        "options": [
            {"airline": "ANA", "price_usd": 850, "duration_h": 14},
            {"airline": "JAL", "price_usd": 920, "duration_h": 13},
            {"airline": "United", "price_usd": 780, "duration_h": 15},
        ],
    }

async def search_hotels(city: str, checkin: str, checkout: str) -> dict:
    """Search for hotels in a city for a date range.

    Args:
        city: City name.
        checkin: Check-in date YYYY-MM-DD.
        checkout: Check-out date YYYY-MM-DD.
    """
    await asyncio.sleep(0.25)
    return {
        "city": city,
        "checkin": checkin,
        "checkout": checkout,
        "options": [
            {"name": "Park Hyatt Tokyo", "price_per_night": 480, "rating": 4.8},
            {"name": "Shinjuku Granbell", "price_per_night": 220, "rating": 4.5},
            {"name": "Capsule Hotel Asakusa", "price_per_night": 65, "rating": 4.2},
        ],
    }

def save_itinerary_to_artifact(itinerary_json: str, tool_context: ToolContext) -> dict:
    """Save a generated itinerary as a session artifact (Day 09).

    Args:
        itinerary_json: JSON string of the complete itinerary.
    """
    artifact_name = f"itinerary_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}.json"
    # In production with GcsArtifactService, this writes to gs://bucket/
    # In dev with InMemoryArtifactService, it lives in the session
    tool_context.save_artifact(artifact_name, itinerary_json.encode())
    return {"artifact_name": artifact_name, "saved": True}

def recall_past_trips(user_id: str) -> dict:
    """Look up the user's past trips from memory service (Day 09)."""
    # Mock — in production, query InMemoryMemoryService.search_memory()
    return {
        "past_destinations": ["Paris", "London"],
        "preferred_airlines": ["ANA"],
        "budget_tier": "premium",
    }

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# CALLBACKS (Day 13) — guardrail, audit, recovery
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Module-level audit log (Day 13 exercise pattern)
AUDIT_LOG: list[dict] = []

def travel_guardrail(
    callback_context: CallbackContext,
    llm_request: LlmRequest,
) -> Optional[LlmResponse]:
    """Block requests mentioning competitors or restricted destinations."""
    if not llm_request.contents:
        return None
    last = llm_request.contents[-1]
    if last.role != "user" or not last.parts:
        return None
    text = (last.parts[0].text or "").lower()

    # Restricted destinations (demo: just an example pattern)
    restricted = ["north korea", "crimea", "antartica unauthorized"]
    for r in restricted:
        if r in text:
            print(f"[guardrail] 🚫 blocked — restricted destination: {r}")
            return LlmResponse(
                content=types.Content(
                    role="model",
                    parts=[types.Part(
                        text=f"I'm sorry, but I can't help plan trips to restricted destinations."
                    )],
                )
            )

    # Log allowed request
    invocation_id = callback_context.invocation_id
    print(f"[guardrail] ✅ allowed invocation={invocation_id[:8]}")
    return None

def audit_tool_calls(
    tool: BaseTool,
    args: dict[str, Any],
    tool_context: ToolContext,
    tool_response: dict,
) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Record every tool call to the audit log (Day 13 after_tool)."""
    record = {
        "timestamp": time.time(),
        "tool": tool.name,
        "args": deepcopy(args),
        "user_id": tool_context.session.user_id if hasattr(tool_context, "session") else "unknown",
        "invocation_id": tool_context.invocation_id if hasattr(tool_context, "invocation_id") else "unknown",
        "response_keys": list(tool_response.keys()) if isinstance(tool_response, dict) else None,
    }
    AUDIT_LOG.append(record)
    print(f"[audit] {tool.name} called (#{len(AUDIT_LOG)} total)")
    return None  # don't modify the response

_failure_count = 0

def graceful_model_recovery(
    callback_context: CallbackContext,
    llm_request: LlmRequest,
    error: Exception,
) -> Optional[LlmResponse]:
    """Graceful fallback on model errors (Day 13 on_model_error)."""
    global _failure_count
    _failure_count += 1
    print(f"[recovery] model error #{_failure_count}: {type(error).__name__}: {error}")

    if _failure_count >= 3:
        print("[recovery] 🔌 circuit breaker — returning maintenance message")
        return LlmResponse(
            content=types.Content(
                role="model",
                parts=[types.Part(
                    text="I'm experiencing technical difficulties. "
                         "Please try again in a few minutes."
                )],
            )
        )

    error_str = str(error).lower()
    if "quota" in error_str or "429" in error_str:
        return LlmResponse(
            content=types.Content(
                role="model",
                parts=[types.Part(
                    text="I'm handling too many requests right now. "
                         "Please wait a moment and try again."
                )],
            )
        )
    return None  # let unknown errors propagate

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SUB-AGENTS (Day 10) — single_turn workers
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

weather_agent = LlmAgent(
    name="weather_agent",
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",
    description="Fetches weather forecasts for travel destinations.",
    instruction=(
        "You are a weather specialist. Use get_weather to fetch the forecast. "
        "Return a concise summary suitable for inclusion in a travel plan."
    ),
    tools=[get_weather],
    output_key="weather_result",  # Day 07 — saves to session.state
    after_tool_callback=audit_tool_calls,
    on_model_error_callback=graceful_model_recovery,
)

flight_agent = LlmAgent(
    name="flight_agent",
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",
    description="Searches for flights between cities.",
    instruction=(
        "You are a flight search specialist. Use search_flights. "
        "Return the top 3 options with airline, price, and duration."
    ),
    tools=[search_flights],
    output_key="flight_result",
    after_tool_callback=audit_tool_calls,
    on_model_error_callback=graceful_model_recovery,
)

hotel_agent = LlmAgent(
    name="hotel_agent",
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",
    description="Searches for hotels in a destination city.",
    instruction=(
        "You are a hotel search specialist. Use search_hotels. "
        "Return the top 3 options with name, price/night, and rating."
    ),
    tools=[search_hotels],
    output_key="hotel_result",
    after_tool_callback=audit_tool_calls,
    on_model_error_callback=graceful_model_recovery,
)

# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# COORDINATOR (Day 10) — routes to sub-agents, aggregates results
# ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

root_agent = LlmAgent(
    name="travel_planner",
    model="gemini-2.0-flash",
    description=(
        "Plans complete trips: weather, flights, and hotels. "
        "Delegates to specialized sub-agents and synthesizes results."
    ),
    instruction=(
        "You are a travel planning coordinator. When a user describes a trip:\n"
        "1. Delegate weather lookup to weather_agent\n"
        "2. Delegate flight search to flight_agent\n"
        "3. Delegate hotel search to hotel_agent\n"
        "4. Once all three return, synthesize a final travel plan\n\n"
        "Use recall_past_trips to personalize recommendations.\n"
        "Use save_itinerary_to_artifact to persist the final plan.\n\n"
        "Available state keys after sub-agents run:\n"
        "  {{weather_result}} — weather summary\n"
        "  {{flight_result}} — flight options\n"
        "  {{hotel_result}} — hotel options\n"
    ),
    sub_agents=[weather_agent, flight_agent, hotel_agent],
    tools=[recall_past_trips, save_itinerary_to_artifact],
    # Day 13 — guardrail runs before every LLM call
    before_model_callback=travel_guardrail,
    after_tool_callback=audit_tool_calls,
    on_model_error_callback=graceful_model_recovery,
    # Day 02 — generate_content_config
    generate_content_config=types.GenerateContentConfig(
        temperature=0.4,
        max_output_tokens=800,
        top_p=0.9,
    ),
    # Day 07 — final synthesized plan saved to state
    output_key="final_itinerary",
)

print(f"✓ Capstone agent ready: {root_agent.name}")
print(f"  Sub-agents: {[a.name for a in root_agent.sub_agents]}")
print(f"  Tools: {[t.name if hasattr(t,'name') else t.__name__ for t in root_agent.tools]}")
print(f"  Callbacks: before_model, after_tool, on_model_error")
```

**Output**

```text
✓ Capstone agent ready: travel_planner\n  Sub-agents: ['weather_agent', 'flight_agent', 'hotel_agent']\n  Tools: ['recall_past_trips', 'save_itinerary_to_artifact']\n  Callbacks: before_model, after_tool, on_model_error\n
```

### main.py — Deploy-ready FastAPI server

Drop this file next to `agent.py` and run `uvicorn main:app`. The agent uses SQLite for sessions (swap for `agentengine://` in prod), file-based artifacts (swap for `gs://`), and in-memory memory (swap for `rag://`).

```python
# travel_planner/main.py — FastAPI deployment entry point (Day 15)
import os
import uvicorn
from google.adk.cli.fast_api import get_fast_api_app

AGENT_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# Production: swap these for managed services
SESSION_SERVICE_URI = os.getenv(
    "SESSION_SERVICE_URI",
    "sqlite+aiosqlite:///./travel_sessions.db",
)
ARTIFACT_SERVICE_URI = os.getenv(
    "ARTIFACT_SERVICE_URI",
    "file://./artifacts/",
)
ALLOWED_ORIGINS = os.getenv(
    "ALLOWED_ORIGINS",
    "http://localhost:3000,http://localhost:8080",
).split(",")

app = get_fast_api_app(
    agents_dir=AGENT_DIR,
    session_service_uri=SESSION_SERVICE_URI,
    artifact_service_uri=ARTIFACT_SERVICE_URI,
    allow_origins=ALLOWED_ORIGINS,
    web=True,  # serve Web UI alongside REST API
)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    uvicorn.run(
        app,
        host="0.0.0.0",
        port=int(os.environ.get("PORT", 8080)),
        log_level="info",
    )
```

**Output**


💡 Key Concept

The capstone is **production-shaped, not production-ready**. Before shipping: (1) swap mock tools for real APIs (Amadeus, Booking.com, OpenWeatherMap); (2) swap SQLite for Postgres or `agentengine://`; (3) swap `file://` artifacts for `gs://`; (4) swap `InMemoryMemoryService` for `rag://`; (5) add user authentication; (6) write eval cases for happy-path and edge-case trips; (7) wire `--trace_to_cloud` and `--otel_to_cloud`; (8) add `ReflectAndRetryModelPlugin` for self-healing. Each swap is a one-line URI or plugin change — the architecture is sound.

⚠️ Important

**Don't ship the mock data to production.** The `mock = {"Tokyo": ...}` dicts in the tools are placeholders. Replace them with real API calls (Amadeus for flights, Booking.com for hotels, OpenWeatherMap for weather) before any user touches this. The architecture is correct — only the data layer needs upgrading.

🚀 Pro Tip

**Fork this capstone for your own domain.** Swap "travel planner" for "code reviewer" (sub-agents: linter, security scanner, test runner), "research assistant" (sub-agents: web search, paper fetcher, summarizer), or "customer support" (sub-agents: order lookup, refund processor, FAQ search). The coordinator + single_turn sub-agents + persistent state + callbacks pattern is universal — only the tools and instructions change.

sections.title: Day 15 Summary
sections.body:
📌 Key Takeaways

- **Cloud Run is the recommended default** for Python ADK deployment — `adk deploy cloud_run` gives you HTTPS URL + autoscaling in 5 minutes

- **Service URI schemes** are universal: `agentengine://`, `gs://`, `rag://`, `sqlite+aiosqlite://` — pick once per environment, reuse across CLI commands

- **Agent Runtime** is for event-driven agents — `--trigger_sources=pubsub,eventarc` registers trigger endpoints

- **Custom FastAPI** via `get_fast_api_app()` is the escape hatch for non-Google-Cloud or full-control deployments

- **Observability stack**: `--trace_to_cloud` + `--otel_to_cloud` + `BigQueryAgentAnalyticsPlugin` + `ReflectAndRetryModelPlugin` + `LoggingPlugin`

- **v2.7.0 breaking change**: install `google-adk[bigquery-analytics]` explicitly — `pyarrow` moved out of `[gcp]`

- **Production checklist**: persistent sessions, GCS artifacts, RAG memory, observability, guardrails, error callbacks, eval gate, scaling, auth

- **The capstone pattern** — coordinator + single_turn sub-agents + `output_key` + callbacks + persistent state — generalizes to almost any multi-agent product

sections.body:
You went from `pip install google-adk` to deploying a production-shaped multi-agent system to Google Cloud.
You can now build agents with the same framework that powers Google's own products. This is the end of the course — and the beginning of your building journey.

### 📚 The Full Journey

Day ·
Topic ·

Day 01 · **ADK Foundations — Install, Architecture & First Agent** ·

Day 02 · **LlmAgent Deep Dive — Parameters, Instructions & Config** ·

Day 03 · **Invocation Flow — Runner, Sessions & Events** ·

Day 04 · **Function Tools — Sync, Async, Long-Running & Parallel** ·

Day 05 · **ToolContext — State, Artifacts, Auth, Escalation** ·

Day 06 · **MCP Integration — McpToolset (Stdio + HTTP)** ·

Day 07 · **Session State — Prefix Scopes & output_key** ·

Day 08 · **Session Services — InMemory, Database, VertexAi** ·

Day 09 · **Memory & Artifacts — Long-term Recall & Binary Storage** ·

Day 10 · **Multi-Agent Systems — Sub-agents, AgentTool, Collaboration** ·

Day 11 · **Workflow Agents — Sequential, Parallel, Loop** ·

Day 12 · **Graph Workflow — Declarative Nodes & Edges** ·

Day 13 · **Callbacks — All 8 Types & Chaining** ·

Day 14 · **ADK Web UI, A2A Protocol & MCP Server Mode** ·

Day 15 · **Deployment & Capstone — Cloud Run, Agent Engine & Production** ·

### 🚀 What to Build Next

Five capstone-sized project ideas, each combining multiple concepts from the course:

- **Customer Support Agent** — Multi-tier support system with order lookup, refund tools, FAQ search, and escalation to human agents via Slack. Deploy to Cloud Run with Postgres sessions.

- **Code Reviewer Bot** — GitHub PR analyzer with sub-agents for linting, security scanning, test coverage, and PR-description quality. Trigger via Eventarc on PR open.

- **Research Assistant** — Multi-source research agent with web search, arXiv fetcher, PDF summarizer, and citation graph builder. Export artifacts as annotated bibliographies.

- **Personal Finance Coach** — Transaction categorizer with sub-agents for budgeting, investment research, and tax optimization. Persist data with RAG memory for multi-year trend analysis.

- **Multi-Agent Game Master** — Tabletop RPG orchestrator with sub-agents for dice rolling, NPC dialogue, combat resolution, and narrative pacing. A2A-exposed so external tools can join the game.

### 🧭 Next Learning Steps

1. **Contribute to ADK** — the project is open-source at [github.com/google/adk-python](https://github.com/google/adk-python). Good first issues are tagged `good-first-issue`. Fixing docs typos and adding examples is a great entry point.
2. **Build a real project end-to-end** — pick one of the 5 ideas above and ship it. Real users will teach you more than any course.
3. **Get Google Cloud certified** — the [Google Cloud Professional Cloud Architect](https://cloud.google.com/learn/certification/cloud-architect) and [Professional Machine Learning Engineer](https://cloud.google.com/learn/certification/machine-learning-engineer) certs complement ADK skills for production roles.
4. **Deepen on observability** — read the [OpenTelemetry specification](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/), set up Jaeger locally, and trace your capstone end-to-end.
5. **Explore adjacent frameworks** — ADK interoperates with LangChain (via tool wrappers), MCP (covered Day 14), and A2A (covered Day 14). Pick one to go deep on.
6. **Stay current** — ADK releases roughly monthly. Watch the [releases page](https://github.com/google/adk-python/releases) and the [adk.dev docs](https://adk.dev). v2.7.0 (August 2026) was a correctness release; expect v2.8+ to add new capabilities.
